kind: CRUD gap G2 (CRUD standard, owner scope of 5 Nov 2026): a sample-invoice payment entered in error can be reversed. One additive migration; sample money only.
findingsNote: No GAP id is created or changed. This PR closes audit gap G2 in docs/revamp/crud/summary.md; the Conductor updates that record.
sensitive: yes: money (sample invoices only, synthetic workspaces), a database migration and a staff command. No auth, session, tenant-scope, consent, token or cookie code changes. Nothing is installed anywhere by this PR; the migration is additive and the owner merges. ADR-061 amendment (payments and reversals) is written by the Conductor.
ownerDecision: Conductor's reading; owner to confirm at merge: sample invoices take a single staff person with a required reason; second-person approval applies to REAL money only (G3, a separate PR).
changed: packages/db/customer-invoicing-migrations/0002_payment_reversal.sql (new, additive): table invoicing_payment_reversal (append-only, one reversal per payment, reason of at least 20 characters starting with Synthetic, rewrite and delete refused, row security on, no runtime or auth access); a guard for every writer; the command log accepts the operation reverse; invoicing_paid, invoicing_position, invoicing_invoice_json, invoicing_emit, app.invoicing_staff_view and app.invoicing_staff_command are replaced with the same signatures and grants.
packages/db/src/customer-invoicing-migrate.ts: runs every file in the folder in order and refuses a changed or missing applied file, as the real-invoicing runner already does.
packages/delivery/src/customer-invoicing-staff.ts: the staff command schema accepts action reverse (invoice, position, payment number, reason).
apps/web/app/operator/customer-invoicing.tsx: a Reverse Payment form (choose an unreversed payment, give a reason) and reversed payments marked in the list with the reason.
packages/auth/src/customer-invoicing.ts and apps/web/app/account/billing/invoices-section.tsx: customers see that a payment was reversed, never why.

tests: tests/integration/customer-invoicing.test.ts (new reversal test; migration history now has two files; a fully paid invoice offers reverse), tests/operator/v3-invoicing-ui.spec.ts (staff reversal flow with a lost answer retried, customer view).
preserved: Payments, credits and invoices stay append-only: the payment row is never edited or deleted, and stays readable with its reversal.
Exact money: amounts stay whole minor units as text; what is paid is derived, never stored; currencies are never added or converted.
Every existing command, guard, event kind and customer read behaves as before; the ordering, over-payment and over-credit guards use the new net paid amount.
A reversal event carries ids and a sequence only, never the amount, the date or the reason.

behaviour.afterReversal: The reversed amount is owed again: paid goes down by it, outstanding goes up by it, and the invoice can be paid, credited or reversed further. A payment is reversed once.
behaviour.position: Reversals count in the invoice position, so a stale screen is refused with 'reload and try again', like payments and credits.
behaviour.actions: Staff view offers reverse while an unreversed payment exists. An invoice that was fully paid now lists reverse; the one existing test that expected an empty list now expects reverse.

reviewFixes: Guardian review of 8d53562: the staff billing route now sends reverse to the invoicing command and stops at the invoicing switch (route-level test added); Reverse Payment asks once in a dialog that names the payment, amount, date and invoice, says it cannot be undone and focuses Keep Payment, and a resend after a lost answer keeps the same command id; the reverse-twice SQL test is three inserts each matching its own error; payment_reversal joins the restricted-login table loop; two reversals of one payment at once record exactly one.
nextAction: G3: real-invoice payments and reversals with a second staff person (money, Sensitive: yes, migration, owner merges).
